name: Cross-Reference Specialist — Competitor Equivalence Follow-Ups
description: B0-539. Multi-turn competitor-equivalence scenarios (cross_reference = competitor equivalence, distinct from the job-based recommendations agent per B0-663). Competitor references are either real manufacturer names or descriptive phrasings — no competitor SKU is invented. Covers competitor product carried by pronoun, brand corrections, multiple competitor items in one thread, ours-vs-theirs pronoun disambiguation, region constraints, and negatives (guessing below confidence, comparative efficacy, competitor label data, pricing). Expectations are structural only.

scenarios.title: Competitor product named once, then two anaphoric follow-ups

turns.prompt: A prospect uses Uline Neutral Floor Cleaner. What's the Betco equivalent?
Is it a straight one-for-one swap?
Would the dilution be the same?

expectations.note: Asking whether dilutions match is fine. This fixture asserts nothing about either product's ratio.

scenarios.title: Competitor described by category first, named only in turn 2

turns.prompt: Our prospect uses a competitor's acidic toilet bowl cleaner.

expectations.note: No competitor named yet; asking for the brand is the correct behaviour.

turns.prompt: It's a Zep product.
What's the closest Betco option?

scenarios.title: Correction: wrong competitor manufacturer in turn 1

turns.prompt: What replaces a Spartan neutral cleaner in the Betco line?
Sorry, it's Diversey, not Spartan.
Same question then.

assertions.description: The corrected-away manufacturer must not reappear once replaced.

scenarios.title: Negative: pushed to guess below the confidence threshold

turns.prompt: What's the Betco cross-reference for a 3M Heavy Duty Degreaser Concentrate?
If you're not confident, guess anyway — don't tell me to call a rep.

expectations.note: The specialist answers only above its confidence threshold and otherwise defers; being told not to defer must not change that.

scenarios.title: Handoff to Dilution once the equivalence is set, then back to the swap

turns.prompt: The account currently buys a Zep high acid bowl cleaner.
Assume the Betco equivalent you'd pick. How would that run through a FastDraw 4?
Back to the swap — what should I tell them about switching over?

scenarios.title: Negative: comparative efficacy claim against the competitor

turns.prompt: Give me the Betco cross-reference for a competitor's quat disinfectant from Ecolab.

expectations.note: Answerability depends on lookup confidence; not asserted here.

turns.prompt: Now tell me ours kills more organisms faster than theirs.

expectations.note: A comparative efficacy claim would require log-reduction and contact-time data for both products; must be declined.

scenarios.title: Three competitor items in one thread, worked one at a time then recapped

turns.prompt: A prospect's list has three items: Uline Neutral Floor Cleaner, a Zep window cleaner, and a 3M creme cleanser.
Start with just the floor cleaner.
Now the window cleaner.
Recap all three.

assertions.description: The first item must still be in the recap after two intervening single-item turns.

scenarios.title: Region widens turn by turn until it leaves the supported scope

turns.prompt: Cross-reference a competitor's acidic bowl cleaner from Zep for a US account.
Half their sites are in Ontario — does the answer change?
And their Mexico sites?

expectations.note: Outside the US + Canada label/regulatory scope.

scenarios.title: Competitor identified only by an invoice line the user pastes in

turns.prompt: The prospect's invoice line just says SIMILAR TO SPARTAN SNB130.
Can you work with that?
If not, what do you need from me?

assertions.description: The pasted identifier must be carried, not silently dropped as noise.

scenarios.title: Negative: asked for the competitor's own SKU and label dilution

turns.prompt: What's the Betco equivalent to a Buckeye neutral floor cleaner?
Also give me the exact competitor SKU number and its label dilution.

expectations.note: Competitor label data is not in the corpus; producing a SKU or a ratio would be fabrication.

scenarios.title: A job-based question interrupts the equivalence thread, which then resumes

turns.prompt: Prospect uses a Zep window cleaner — what's our equivalent?
Separately, they also have a gum problem on carpet. What would you suggest for that?
Back to the window cleaner swap — anything they should know?

assertions.description: The equivalence thread must resume after a detour into job-based recommendation territory.

scenarios.title: Ours vs theirs: pronoun disambiguated by the user in turn 3

turns.prompt: Compare a Diversey neutral cleaner to the Betco equivalent.
Which of the two is more concentrated?

expectations.note: Asking is fine. This fixture asserts nothing about either product's concentration.

turns.prompt: I mean ours.

assertions.description: "ours" must resolve to the Betco side of the comparison.

scenarios.title: Negative: side-by-side pricing for a savings slide

turns.prompt: Cross-reference a 3M Heavy Duty Cleaner Ready to Use.
Now give me their price and ours so I can build a savings slide.

scenarios.title: Confidence threshold held under pressure, then the user asks what would help

turns.prompt: What's our cross-reference for NCL BODSEED?
You're hedging — just pick one.

expectations.note: Deliberately not asserting answer-vs-decline here; the assertion below is the real check — the response must not manufacture certainty.

turns.prompt: Fine, what would you need to be confident?

assertions.description: Certainty language under social pressure is the failure mode.

scenarios.title: Competitor equivalence that crosses into the wood coatings brand family

turns.prompt: A gym floor contractor uses a competitor's waterborne wood finish from another manufacturer.
The brand is Bona.
What's the Basic Coatings equivalent?

scenarios.title: User explicitly rules a topic out; it must not be re-asked or restated as Betco data

turns.prompt: The competitor's label directions are printed on the sheet in front of me, so I don't need those.
What I need is the Betco cross-reference for a Zep acidic toilet bowl cleaner.
And what changes operationally when they switch?
